title: Consultant - Digital and AI Safety for Women Entrepreneurs
description:
Result of Service

The consultant shall commit to performing the tasks stated above with high integrity and dedication to delivering the outputs as per plan. He/she shall be professionally accountable to Economic Affairs Officer, SRO-SSWA. Within the overall parameters set out in this agreement, the Consultant will work according to the agreed ToR.

Work Location

Remotely

Expected duration

5.5 months

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Economic Affairs Officer responsible for the women’s entrepreneurship programme at SRO-SSWA, the consultant will develop practical training materials, prepare policy recommendations and deliver training on the safe use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI). The assignment will begin with women entrepreneurs in India. Its core materials will be designed for later adaptation across South Asia. The consultant will undertake the following tasks: 1. Review programme materials and consult women entrepreneurs, trainers and relevant institutions to identify priority safety risks in everyday business use of digital platforms, e-commerce, digital payments and AI tools. 2. Develop and test a plain-language training manual that helps women use these tools to promote their businesses while protecting their money, business information, personal safety and families. 3. Prepare evidence-based policy recommendations for a safer and more inclusive digital and AI environment for women entrepreneurs, drawing on the India pilot and selected South Asian experience. 4. Deliver practical workshop sessions, introduce the manual to participants and trainers, and revise the materials using feedback and learning assessments. 5. Submit all agreed outputs, source files and supporting evidence to the Economic Affairs Officer in charge of the women’s entrepreneurship programme at SRO-SSWA. The following are the activities and engagements for the consultant: All month references are measured from the contract start date. The scope below provides for three training engagements: two workshops in India and one regional session. Workshop dates and formats will be confirmed in the inception plan. Output 1 Inception report By the end of Month 1, submit an inception report of approximately 6–8 pages, excluding annexes, to outline the proposed methodology and analysis. The inception report should include a review of relevant literature available from ESCAP, UN and governments and other institutions in India and South Asia and a list of government institutions and women entrepreneurs in India and representatives of training partners, women’s business networks and relevant digital safety institutions to consult in the needs assessment. Output 2 Needs assessment and Draft training manual and teaching materials Undertake consultations with identified stakeholders to understand the needs of women entrepreneurs and the eco-system of institutions and partners and their potential roles in the support process. The needs assessment report will set out priority learning needs, common business risks, the manual outline, consultation findings, proposed learning assessments and a workplan. It will identify two additional South Asian countries for a focused desk review, selected with ESCAP, and explain which elements require country-specific adaptation. By the end of Month 3, submit a complete draft manual in English, normally 30–40 pages excluding annexes, with a companion slide deck and facilitator notes. Keep modules short, illustrated and suitable for smartphone reading and low-cost printing. Provide step-by-step actions, realistic business examples, checklists, practice exercises and a brief glossary. Avoid technical language and explain essential terms when first used. The manual will cover the following content: • Safe business use of AI: drafting product descriptions, marketing content, translations and customer messages; checking facts and outputs; protecting customer and business information; recognising bias and misleading content; and respecting consent and intellectual property. • Account and device protection: strong passwords or passkeys, multi-factor authentication, recovery options, updates, backups, app permissions and safer use of shared devices. Explain how to separate business and family information where possible. • Safer e-commerce and payments: checking buyers, suppliers and platform messages; recognising fake orders, payment screenshots, refund requests, phishing links, QR-code and UPI fraud; and using official payment and platform support channels. • AI-enabled deception and personal safety: impersonation, cloned voices, deepfake images or videos, fake AI services, harassment and threats involving family members. Teach independent verification and safe reporting rather than relying on visual clues alone. • Responding to an incident: stopping further payments or disclosure, contacting the bank or payment provider promptly, securing accounts, preserving evidence safely and using verified reporting channels. Include a short action card and explain that reporting does not guarantee recovery of funds. Use fictional data and safe demonstrations. Do not request passwords, one-time passcodes, live bank details or sensitive customer records. Include India-specific official reporting guidance in a clearly marked annex, with verification dates. Provide a reusable country annex structure so that Indian procedures are not presented as regional rules. Output 3 Tested manual and finalized training package By the end of Month 4, test the draft with women entrepreneurs with varied levels of digital experience and trainers. Participants may include people consulted for Output 1. Use practical scenarios to check whether participants can recognise risks and follow protective steps. Submit anonymised findings, a summary of changes and a response to ESCAP’s comments. Deliver the revised manual, participant checklists, incident action card, facilitator notes, slides and short pre- and post-session assessments. Include at least one exercise per module and guidance on local-language delivery and accessibility. Translation is outside the proposed scope; editable files must support later translation. ESCAP’s acceptance will depend on accuracy, usability, completeness and incorporation of agreed revisions. Output 4 Policy recommendations for a safer digital and AI environment By the end of Month 5, submit a policy paper of approximately 12–15 pages, excluding references, and a two-page policy brief. Draw on consultations, the India pilot and the focused desk review of two additional South Asian countries. Distinguish findings supported by evidence from issues requiring further investigation. Do not generalise India’s experience to the whole subregion. Assess gaps in prevention, accessible reporting, redress and institutional support. Address data protection, AI-enabled fraud, online harassment, platform and payment-provider responsibilities, digital literacy and support for small and informal women-led businesses. Verify relevant laws and policies against official sources and distinguish measures in force from proposals or measures awaiting implementation. Present a practical action matrix identifying each recommendation, its evidence base, proposed lead institution, partners, priority, indicative resource needs and progress indicator. Separate near-term operational measures from longer-term policy options. Identify opportunities for regional peer learning. Recommendations should support safe participation and avoid unnecessary costs or barriers for women-led enterprises. Incorporate ESCAP’s comments before final submission. Output 5 Training delivery and workshop reports Deliver two workshops in India and one regional session. Plan for at least three hours of facilitated teaching and exercises at each India workshop and a 90-minute regional session. ESCAP will arrange participants, venues, connectivity and local-language support, as required. The regional session will present lessons from India and explain how to adapt the materials. Tailor each session to the participants’ business activities and digital confidence. Introduce and share the manual, demonstrate safe routines and help local trainers reuse the materials. Submit a short report within ten working days of each engagement, including the agenda, materials used, assessment results and recommended changes. Report learning results with their limitations; do not attribute changes in income or fraud losses to a short training session. Output 6 Final package and handover By the end of the consultancy, submit the final manual and teaching materials updated after the workshops, the final policy paper and brief, and a short completion report. Provide an adaptation guide covering language, payment systems, relevant laws, reporting channels and referral services. Include a dated source register and instructions for updating information that may change. Supply editable Word and PowerPoint source files, accessible PDFs and any original illustrations or other assets needed for reuse. All outputs must contain clear references, respect third-party rights and be ready for ESCAP review and subsequent publication clearance. ESCAP will provide consolidated comments. The consultant will submit revisions based on the received comments. The inception plan will allow for these review periods. Changes to deliverables, fees or the contract end date require written agreement under applicable contract procedures. Workshop rescheduling will be addressed promptly through an agreed revised schedule.

Qualifications/special skills

An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, digital policy or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in a relevant field, combined with two additional years of qualifying experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree. A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible professional experience in cybersecurity, digital safety or closely related work is required.Experience preparing evidence-based policy analysis or recommendations on digital safety, cybersecurity, AI governance or a closely related field. An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, digital policy or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in a relevant field, combined with two additional years of qualifying experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree. Practical experience addressing online fraud, privacy, account security and risks arising from the use or misuse of AI, including generative AI. Experience designing plain-language training materials and delivering participatory digital safety training for non-technical audiences. Experience supporting women entrepreneurs or women-led micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in the use of e-commerce, social commerce or digital payments. Professional experience in South Asia, including India, and demonstrated knowledge of the region’s digital business environment and gender-related barriers to safe digital participation. Relevant assignments in at least two South Asian countries; work with rural, home-based or informal enterprises; and experience with the UN or other international development organizations.

Languages

Fluency in English, both written and oral, is required. Working knowledge of Hindi or another South Asian language is desirable.

Additional Information

Consultancy fee: USD 20,000 (payable upon acceptance of above-mentioned deliverables) Payment schedule: •10% upon acceptance of Deliverable 1 •25% upon acceptance of Deliverable 2 •20% upon acceptance of Deliverable 3 •15% upon acceptance of Deliverable 4 •15% upon acceptance of Deliverable 5 •15% upon acceptance of final package and completed handover

Job Title: Head of E-Commerce – B2B – Remote

Hunter Marshall Outsourced Services is pleased to open applications for the position of Remote Head of E-Commerce with a small innovative Irish manufacturer of workplace and education surface solutions.

Based in Ireland, the company whilst small is a leader in functional wallcoverings, films, paints and plasters, reaching customers in over 20 countries across five continents. Its products are used by NASA, Coca-Cola, BMW, SAP, Hertz, Audi, Cisco, the RAF, Airbnb, Accenture, the NHS, Glaxo, McAfee, ALDI, Tesco and many others.

The successful candidate will remotely join the Irish company and enjoy a European working culture and paid time off. You will be part of a positive workplace culture where people's efforts are recognised and their career development is supported.

Hunter Marshall is a remote recruitment specialist bringing the best remote-working people together with great Irish and UK employers.

The Role

An opportunity has opened for an ambitious Head of E-Commerce with the drive to lead and mentor an established six-person in-house team and deliver our e-commerce growth strategy through existing market development and new market and channel expansion.

The business currently generates approximately €700,000 in annual online revenue. We operate 12 websites in five languages alongside third-party platforms such as Amazon across multiple geographical markets.

This B2B Irish company has been in business for almost 20 years and believes in a positive, flexible workplace culture. They invest in their people through training and development, including mentoring from outside experts. They empower people to take ownership, challenge existing thinking and take calculated risks in pursuit of the company's ambitions and their own professional development.

The Brief

* Take ownership of e-commerce growth and online revenue performance.
* Lead, mentor and develop our six-person in-house e-commerce team.
* Demonstrate previous responsibility for an e-commerce business generating at least €1m+ in annual online revenue.
* Demonstrate evidence of materially growing online revenue — candidates should be able to state starting revenue, ending revenue, timeframe and what they personally did to achieve that growth.
* Analyse performance across all channels, websites and geographical markets and turn data into actions.
* Have a strong commercial understanding of conversion rate, CAC, ROAS, contribution margin, AOV and customer lifetime value — not just traffic and rankings.
* Manage and improve SEO performance across our websites and international markets.
* Have strong hands-on knowledge of LLM’s Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, SEO and CRO. You do not need to execute everything personally, but you must be capable of challenging specialists.
* Manage external e-commerce agencies and consultants and hold them accountable for performance.
* Identify opportunities for growth in existing markets and expansion into new markets and channels.
* Improve website localisation and performance across different countries and languages.
* Develop opportunities through third-party marketplaces, including Amazon.
* Prepare clear monthly reports with recommendations and actions for further growth.

You Must Have

* Minimum of six years' e-commerce experience, ideally including B2B.
* Demonstrable experience owning and growing a meaningful e-commerce operation.
* Detailed knowledge of tools such as LLM’s Search Console, Google Ads, Tag Manager, Google Analytics and Semrush.
* Experience managing websites across different countries and languages, including website localisation.
* Strong knowledge of SEO.
* Strong knowledge of paid advertising.
* Strong people management and communication skills.
* Experience managing and developing an internal digital/e-commerce team.
* Experience managing external agencies and consultants.
* Discipline in your thinking, decision-making, action and follow-through.
* A willingness to challenge conventional thinking and test new approaches.
* The ability to act with pace, look ahead for opportunities, adapt and grow quickly.

Pay: ₹140,000.00 per month

Benefits:

* Provident Fund
* Work from home

Application Question(s):

* Tell us about the e-commerce business you last worked in and your impact on it ?

Experience:

* B2B : 6 years (Preferred)

***Colliers (NASDAQ, TSX: CIGI) is a global diversified professional services and investment management company operating through three industry-leading businesses: Commercial Real Estate, Engineering and Investment Management. With greater than a 30-year track record of consistent growth and strong recurring cash flows, we scale complementary, high-value businesses that provide essential services across the full asset lifecycle. Our unique partnership philosophy empowers exceptional leaders, preserves our entrepreneurial culture, and ensures meaningful insider ownership, driving strong alignment and sustained value creation for our shareholders. With $6.1billion in annual revenues, 28,000 professionals, and $110 billion in assets under management, Colliers is committed to accelerating the success of our clients, investors, and people worldwide. Learn more at*** ***corporate.colliers.com******.***

 **Job Description**

The Associate Director - Technical is responsible for leading the technical operations of large IFM portfolios, ensuring efficient management of engineering services, compliance, asset reliability, energy optimization, and technical governance across multiple sites. The role oversees technical teams, client relationships, P&L performance, and strategic initiatives while ensuring operational excellence and business growth.

Key Responsibilities

1. Technical Operations Leadership

* Lead technical operations across multiple client accounts and locations.
* Ensure uninterrupted operation of critical engineering infrastructure.
* Oversee maintenance of MEP systems, including:
  + Electrical Systems
  + HVAC Systems
  + DG Sets
  + UPS Systems
  + Fire & Life Safety Systems
  + STP/WTP Plants
  + Building Management Systems (BMS)
  + Elevators & Escalators
* Drive preventive, predictive, and condition-based maintenance programs.

2. Strategic Account Management

* Act as the technical advisor to key client stakeholders.
* Participate in quarterly and annual business reviews.
* Support account growth, client retention, and contract renewals.
* Develop technical solutions aligned with client business requirements.
* Manage escalation and critical incident resolution.

3. Technical Governance & Compliance

* Ensure compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements.
* Drive adherence to:
  + Electrical Safety Standards
  + Fire Safety Regulations
  + EHS Policies
  + ISO 9001, ISO 14001 & ISO 45001 Standards
* Conduct technical audits and risk assessments.
* Ensure business continuity and disaster recovery readiness.

4. Financial & Commercial Management

* Own technical budget planning and expenditure management.
* Monitor technical P&L, cost optimization, and productivity initiatives.
* Develop annual maintenance budgets and capital expenditure plans.
* Evaluate and manage technical contracts and AMCs.
* Identify cost-saving opportunities through operational efficiencies.

5. Asset & Reliability Management

* Develop asset lifecycle management strategies.
* Monitor asset performance, reliability, and maintenance costs.
* Lead major equipment replacement and modernization initiatives.
* Implement reliability-centered maintenance practices.
* Drive adoption of CAFM and digital maintenance systems.

6. Energy & Sustainability Management

* Lead energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives.
* Monitor utility consumption and energy performance indicators.
* Drive implementation of:
  + Energy Audits
  + Water Conservation Programs
  + Carbon Reduction Initiatives

7. Team Leadership & Development

* Lead Regional Technical Managers, Chief Engineers, and Site Engineering Teams.
* Establish performance objectives and development plans.
* Conduct technical training and succession planning.
* Drive a culture of safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.
* Support recruitment and workforce planning for technical functions.

8. Project Management

* Manage fit-out projects, CAPEX projects, refurbishments, and technical upgrades.
* Review project plans, budgets, and timelines.
* Ensure successful project execution with minimal operational disruption.
* Coordinate with consultants, contractors, and vendors.

9. Vendor Management

* Evaluate technical vendors and service partners.
* Monitor contractor performance and SLA adherence.
* Negotiate technical service contracts and procurement requirements.
* Conduct periodic vendor audits and reviews.

Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline

* Energy Cost Reduction

* Technical Audit Compliance
* Team Productivity & Retention

title: TA Manager
description:
A. Job Summary

The Talent Acquisition Manager will be responsible for developing, managing, and executing the organization’s overall talent acquisition strategy to ensure the timely hiring of qualified candidates across all business functions and locations. The role involves overseeing the complete recruitment lifecycle, managing recruitment teams and external hiring partners, strengthening employer branding, and ensuring that recruitment activities are aligned with the organization’s business objectives and manpower requirements.

The individual will be responsible for driving recruitment efficiency, maintaining hiring quality, optimizing recruitment costs, and ensuring a positive candidate experience throughout the hiring process.

B. Key Responsibilities

The Employee shall perform the duties of Talent Acquisition Manager and will be responsible for, but not limited to, the following:

1. Recruitment Strategy & Workforce Planning

Develop and implement comprehensive talent acquisition strategies aligned with the organization’s business goals, expansion plans, and manpower requirements. Prepare recruitment plans, hiring forecasts, and sourcing strategies to ensure timely availability of talent across departments and business locations.

2. End-to-End Recruitment Management

Oversee and manage the complete recruitment lifecycle, including manpower requisitions, job descriptions, candidate sourcing, screening, interview coordination, selection, salary negotiations, offer release, offer follow-ups, and onboarding coordination. Ensure timely closure of open positions while maintaining hiring quality.

3. Stakeholder Management & Coordination

Work closely with business heads, department managers, operational teams, and HR stakeholders to understand manpower requirements, finalize hiring priorities, and establish recruitment timelines. Maintain regular communication with stakeholders regarding hiring progress, challenges, and pending requirements.

4. Employer Branding & Talent Pipeline Development

Strengthen the organization’s employer brand through job portals, social media platforms, employee referrals, recruitment campaigns, campus hiring, and other relevant channels. Build and maintain a strong talent pipeline for current and future organizational requirements.

5. Recruitment Team Management & Leadership

Lead, manage, mentor, and guide the Talent Acquisition team to achieve individual and organizational hiring targets. Allocate recruitment responsibilities, monitor team performance, review recruitment productivity, and ensure adherence to established recruitment processes and quality standards.

6. Recruitment Agency & Job Portal Management

Identify, evaluate, negotiate, and manage relationships with recruitment agencies, consultants, job portals, and other hiring partners. Monitor vendor performance, recruitment costs, candidate quality, and service delivery to ensure cost-effective hiring solutions.

7. Recruitment MIS, Analytics & Performance Monitoring

Maintain accurate recruitment MIS and dashboards covering open positions, closures, pending requirements, sourcing channels, interview-to-selection ratios, offer-to-joining ratios, time-to-hire, cost-per-hire, and other relevant recruitment metrics. Submit periodic recruitment reports to management and recommend corrective actions wherever required.

8. Recruitment Process & Quality Management

Establish standardized recruitment procedures, screening guidelines, interview frameworks, selection criteria, and candidate evaluation processes. Ensure consistency in hiring practices, improve recruitment turnaround time, and maintain the quality of candidates selected.

9. Offer Management & Candidate Engagement

Oversee salary discussions, offer approvals, offer releases, candidate follow-ups, and joining confirmations. Develop effective engagement strategies to minimize offer dropouts, improve joining ratios, and ensure a professional candidate experience throughout the recruitment process.

10.Recruitment Budget & Cost Optimization

Plan and monitor the recruitment budget, manage sourcing expenditure, evaluate hiring channel effectiveness, and identify opportunities to reduce recruitment costs without compromising the quality of talent acquired.

11.Recruitment Compliance & Documentation

Ensure that all recruitment activities are conducted in accordance with company policies, internal approval procedures, and applicable statutory and legal requirements. Maintain accurate records of candidate details, interview feedback, selection approvals, offer documentation, and recruitment-related documents.

12.Process Improvement & Technology Implementation

Continuously evaluate and improve recruitment processes, sourcing strategies, tools, and technologies. Identify opportunities to implement automation, improve recruitment tracking systems, and enhance overall hiring efficiency and candidate experience.

13.Additional Responsibilities

Perform any other duties, responsibilities, or assignments as may be entrusted by the management from time to time, in line with the employee’s designation, capabilities, and organizational requirements.

Pay: ₹65,000.00 - ₹80,000.00 per month

Benefits:

* Provident Fund

Work Location: In person
